rows.question: According to the student handbook, may generative AI be a student's only source for preparatory research?

relevant.section: 4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools

rows.expect: It may help with preparatory research, but it must not be the only source.

response.answer:
4. [academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf / 4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools]
Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools In general, using Generative AI tools for preparatory research work, assignment and project is considered acceptable practice, however such tools should never be the only source of information used. [academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf / 4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools]
Generative AI tools are not academic sources; they do not produce fact- checked content, and they can, and often do, reproduce inherent biases in provision of information, and they often do not accurately state the sources from which the content provided has been gathered. [academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf / 4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools]
It is therefore vital that students use academic and trusted disciplinary- specific sources when developing their work. [academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf / 4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools]
None of the content generated by AI should be used in submitted work unless it is quoted and referenced as such. [academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf / 4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools]
AI is at its best when it is used to help synthesize ideas, so that users are in a better position to write an assignment. [academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf / 4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools]
It may be helpful for students to consider Generative AI tools in a similar light to Wikipedia: as a source of information, but not always a reliable one. [academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf / 4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools]
See some potentially acceptable uses of Generative AI here. [academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf / 4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools]
Please note, this list is not exhaustive and is indicative only. 1) Initial research into a topic, idea, or concept to gain an overview for example: “what are the main ethical concerns for students when using generative artificial intelligence tools?” [academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf / 4.
